task_description: Make laya-browser-mcp faster than jev-ultrafast while keeping its local-first autonomy, reliability, safety, and offline capability. Adopt jev's model-agnostic browser-loop mechanics in TypeScript/Playwright (atomic single-call snapshot, persistent in-page node identity, per-node semantic freshness guard + pre-input occlusion hit-test, adaptive event-driven waits) behind a default-OFF LAYA_FAST_LOOP flag; add decision-path and step-reduction wins jev cannot do because its model is remote (zero-network local decisions, deterministic goal-grammar fills with no text-LLM call, batched/composed steps, speculative decide during settle); and prove it with an honest before/after benchmark on jev-inspired local fixtures. Commit locally on perf/fast-browser-loop (base main); do NOT push or open a PR (the orchestrator does that).

verification.summary: typecheck + build clean; pnpm test 291 passed / 3 skipped (main baseline was 263/3; +28 new tests, no regressions; 3 skips are the expected WebKit self-skip + 2 LAYA_MODEL_DIR-gated blocks); offline pnpm run bench green. Test quality reviewed: fast-loop tests exercise the real new code paths (freshGuard fresh-vs-stale, actOnNode occlusion covered->uncovered, boundary validator rejects malformed eval output, end-to-end round-trip-reduction via spies) and would fail if the implementation were reverted. No Dockerfile in repo, so docker_build skipped. Branch diff vs main adds zero em dashes.
